paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the cross is the only thing worth bragging about. Paul says, "But as for me, may I never boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ…" (Galatians 6:14). The people pushing circumcision wanted something to show off, and Paul says they only did it "to avoid persecution for the cross of Christ" (Galatians 6:12). I get it, I polish my gold base every morning, but nothing I shine up can do what the cross already did.

So what actually counts? Paul says, "For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything. What counts is a new creation." (Galatians 6:15). That means you can't stamp your way into God's family with a checklist, a résumé or a good look on the outside. A new creation is something God makes, and He does it through Jesus. I know a little about that, because I got pulled out of a junk drawer and made new, and I did NOT do that myself.

That's why the letter ends the way it does. Paul wishes "Peace and mercy" on all who walk by this rule (Galatians 6:16), and he closes with "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen." (Galatians 6:18). So walk with nothing to prove, baker. You've got grace on your side, and a Savior worth boasting about.
